blame.commit_message: Seed bug: add_item() returns list.append()'s result (always None) instead of the cart

hypothesis.root_cause: The add_item() function returns the result of list.append(), which always evaluates to None in Python, instead of returning the updated cart (or cart.items). Any caller that does `cart = add_item(cart, item)` or accesses `.items` on the return value ends up with None, causing the subsequent 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'items' AttributeError when that None value is later used as if it were a cart object.
evidence: Git blame commit 01d5edcc52 is explicitly titled 'Seed bug: add_item() returns list.append()'s result (always None) instead of the cart', confirming this is a known intentionally-seeded bug.
The code at cart.py line 10 is `return cart.items.append(item)` - list.append() always returns None in Python, so add_item() always returns None regardless of input.

The error message 'NoneType' object has no attribute items' matches exactly what would occur if a caller reassigns cart = add_item(cart, item) and then later calls cart.items, since cart would now be None.

The stack trace originates at cart.py:10 inside add_item, consistent with the append call being the point where the None-producing expression is evaluated, though the actual AttributeError likely surfaces on a subsequent line/call using the returned None.
hypothesis.suggested_fix_direction: Modify add_item() to perform cart.items.append(item) as a statement (not return its result) and then explicitly `return cart` (or return cart.items if that's the intended contract), ensuring callers receive a valid cart/list object instead of None.

fix.commit_message: fix: add_item() now returns the updated cart instead of None
fix.summary: add_item() was returning the result of list.append(), which is always None; it now appends as a statement and explicitly returns the cart object so chained calls like `cart = add_item(cart, item)` work correctly.
